positions.position: Existing commands use singular form (quickmark_save, quickmark_add, quickmark_load, bookmark_add, bookmark_load); the new commands should follow that pattern as quickmark_reload and bookmark_reload to match the established naming.
The plural form 'quickmarks_reload'/'bookmarks_reload' reads naturally because the operation acts on the entire collection, not a single mark; consistency matters less than clarity at the call site.

dissents.topic: Whether reload() should preserve in-memory state on parse failure

positions.position: reload() clears self.marks before re-parsing, so a failure in _init_lineparser or _parse_line leaves the user with an empty marks list and a 'changed' signal — should parse into a temp dict first and swap atomically.
The original __init__ also did not guard against parse failures; replicating the existing behavior in reload() is acceptable and keeps the diff minimal.

issues.description: Inconsistent command naming: new commands use plural while all existing mark commands use singular
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark_save, quickmark_add, quickmark_load, quickmark_del, bookmark_add, bookmark_load, bookmark_del, bookmark_list — all singular. The PR introduces quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload (plural). This breaks discoverability via tab completion (users typing `:quickmark<TAB>` won't see the reload command grouped) and breaks naming consistency in the public command surface.

issues.description: reload() clears marks before parsing — a parse error leaves state empty
issues.detail: In urlmarks.py reload() calls self.marks.clear() then iterates the lineparser. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises (e.g., file I/O error, malformed entry causing InvalidUrlError-like handling), the user loses their in-memory marks even though no new state was successfully loaded. Safer: parse into a fresh OrderedDict, then swap on success, then emit changed.

issues.description: Feature file scenarios are missing titles
issues.detail: Both new Gherkin scenarios are declared as bare `Scenario:` with no name. Every other scenario in tests/end2end/features/urlmarks.feature has a descriptive title (e.g., 'Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)'). Unnamed scenarios make test reports harder to read and break the established convention in the file.

issues.description: changed.emit() now fires during __init__ via reload()
issues.detail: Previously __init__ populated self.marks without emitting `changed` (the signal was only fired by add/delete/clear). After this refactor, __init__ calls self.reload() which emits `changed` at construction time. Any slot connected before construction completes won't see it, but any code that later relies on 'changed only fires after a user-initiated modification' may now misbehave. Worth verifying no listeners assume changed is post-init only — and consider not emitting from the initial load path.

issues.description: No doc/changelog entry for the new commands
issues.detail: qutebrowser maintains command documentation (doc/help/commands.asciidoc) and a changelog. The diff adds two new user-visible commands but does not update either. New :commands should be documented and announced for users to discover them.

issues.description: Unit test does not assert clear-before-reload semantics for removed entries
issues.detail: test_reload writes one URL, constructs the manager, then overwrites the file with a different URL and reloads. It asserts the new entry is present but doesn't explicitly verify the original entry was removed (it happens to be the same list length). A stronger test would start with two entries, reload with one, and assert the removed one is gone — guarding the marks.clear() behavior.

issues.description: Blank line between manager.reload() and message.info() is stylistically odd
issues.detail: Both new command methods have an empty line between the reload call and the message.info call. This is a 2-line method and the blank line adds nothing; minor style nit compared to the surrounding command bodies which are tightly packed.

issues.description: _init_lineparser is called again on reload — may re-register or duplicate state
issues.detail: reload() calls self._init_lineparser() each time. Depending on whether LineParser holds open file handles, signals, or a savemanager registration, re-initializing on every reload could leak resources or re-register with the save manager. Worth confirming that LineParser is safe to re-instantiate without cleanup of the previous instance.

issues.description: No PR description text closing an issue or linking the feature request
issues.detail: The PR template prompts for a 'Closes #12345' line. The description is a single sentence with no linked issue. Not a code defect, but qutebrowser PRs typically link to a tracking issue for triage.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful capability — reloading quickmarks/bookmarks from disk — and the refactor of __init__ to delegate to reload() is a clean DRY move. However, the user-facing command names (`quickmarks_reload`, `bookmarks_reload`) break the singular naming convention used by every other mark command, which hurts discoverability and consistency. The reload() implementation clears in-memory state before parsing, so a parse or I/O failure leaves the user with empty marks — it should swap atomically. Tests are unnamed scenarios (against the file's convention) and the unit test could be strengthened to assert removal of stale entries. Docs/changelog updates appear missing for the new commands.
